summary: Invoice contains unexpected background probe thread charges applied to legacy cost center after org split
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLayer reports an unexpected invoice line for 'background probe threads' with non-zero token counts after they completed an org split and cost-center migration. The charge appears on the legacy cost center (BrightLayer-Legacy) instead of the new cost-center (BrightLayer-Prod).

Impact:
- Customer sees a $3,412 line item on their March invoice labeled 'background-probe-threads' (USD).
- Billing affects archived/legacy cost center and caused an internal spend alert for BrightLayer's finance team.
- Customer requests a provisional credit and an explanation of why probe traffic was counted as billable usage during the migration window.

Environment:
- Hosted API (prod-us-west) behind edge ingest-proxy cluster ingest-west-2b.
- Org split performed by BrightLayer on 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) BrightLayer initiated org split and created new cost-center BrightLayer-Prod at ~2026-03-09T21:55 UTC.
2) Automation migrated API keys and tags; some keys were retired and new keys issued.
3) At 2026-03-09T22:05-22:40 UTC, probe threads (automated health-check clients) from edge proxies were routed through older key alias which still referenced BrightLayer-Legacy.
4) Metering pipeline consumed probe telemetry with a 'probe' tag but tag-normalization service mapped that traffic to the legacy cost center due to a name collision in the tag namespace during split.
5) Hourly metering accumulator emitted usage lines that were picked up by the billing pipeline and resulted in the invoice line.

Logs / evidence provided by customer:
- CSV extract of invoice line: invoice_202603.pdf line 42: background-probe-threads | 1,204,800 tokens | $3412.00
- Customer tracing: probe-client logs showing requests at 2026-03-09T22:10:12Z with key alias 'bl-legacy-probe'
- Console screenshot showing workload tagged as 'probe' and cost center 'BrightLayer-Legacy' during the window.

Customer request:
- Immediate provisional credit to remove the line pending reconciliation.
- Root cause explanation and steps taken to prevent re-occurrence.
- Confirmation that historical invoices will be corrected if we find the charge is erroneous.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC - Triage by support: validated invoice line exists and matches token counts from metering archive.
2026-03-10 10:02 UTC - Pulled hourly-accumulator logs for 2026-03-09 22:00-23:00 UTC (ingest-west-2b). Found batches with tag='probe' and cost_center_id pointing to legacy org id 1023.

2026-03-10 11:20 UTC - Tag-normalization service shows a transient namespace collision: 'probe' aliases for bl-probe-* were not fully reconciled after key rename; normalization fell back to existing mapping (legacy) for ~35 minutes.
2026-03-10 12:05 UTC - Checked linked INT-4281 (internal migration-tool bug) which indicates the migration tool omitted alias remap for retired keys when org_id changed.
2026-03-10 13:40 UTC - Confirmed billing pipeline did not apply special probe-exempt policy because probe traffic was tagged as production key in the accumulator output.
Hypothesis: Migration automation omitted alias update for probe clients; normalization fallback assigned legacy cost center; system treated probe threads as billable production traffic.
comments: Support (Maya Patel) - 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: Hi BrightLayer — we're investigating. Can you confirm which API keys were retired and the new key IDs? Also can you share a small sample from your probe client showing the key header?

Customer (Jason Liu, BrightLayer) - 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC: Thanks Maya. We rotated keys via the org-split UI. Sample header attached in the portal as probe_sample_20260309.log (shows key alias bl-legacy-probe). We want a provisional credit while you investigate.

Support (Evelyn Chen) - 2026-03-10 10:15 UTC: Received the sample. We've started pulling accumulator batches and tag-normalization logs. I've filed INT-4281 with infra to confirm migration-tool behavior. Will update within 4 hours.

Infra (Diego Ramos, INT-4281) - 2026-03-10 11:35 UTC: Confirmed migration-tool v2.3.1 has a known edge-case: probe alias entries without explicit org_id were left pointing to previous org. Patch drafted in PR #2412 to include alias remap for retired keys.

Support (Evelyn Chen) - 2026-03-11 08:50 UTC: We have a replicated run in staging that reproduces the alias slip. Preparing steps to backfill meter attribution and request provisional credit. Scheduling billing adjustment job for 2026-03-12 00:00 UTC.
Customer (Jason Liu) - 2026-03-11 12:05 UTC: Appreciate the update. Please confirm timeline for credit appearing on their account and whether future org splits will need manual checks.

Support (Evelyn Chen) - 2026-03-12 07:30 UTC: Billing adjustment submitted for provisional credit. Expect credit to reflect within 3 business days. Migration-tool patch merged; deployment scheduled to staging on 2026-03-12 and prod on 2026-03-13 behind a feature flag.
resolution: 2026-03-12 07:30 UTC - Provisional credit of $3,412 submitted to account ledger as a temporary credit (pending final reconciliation).
2026-03-12 09:40 UTC - Migration-tool patch (metering alias remap) merged to main (PR #2412). Deployment to prod scheduled with feature-flag and rollout plan.

Follow-up actions: Run backfill job to re-attribute tokens from legacy cost center to BrightLayer-Prod for 2026-03-09 21:55-22:40 UTC window; audit the tag-normalization fallback logic to ensure probe traffic with 'probe' tag is marked non-billable when detected as health-checks in future.
Customer notified of provisional credit and timeline for final reconciliation.
next_steps: Schedule and run attribution backfill job (Data Eng) - target: 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC.
Monitor staging rollout of alias-remap patch and run migration-simulation testcases (SRE) - target: 2026-03-12.
Update runbook: org-split checklist must include explicit probe alias remap verification (Docs/Onboarding) - target: 2026-03-14.
Close support ticket after final invoice correction and customer confirmation.
